answers.why: The LORD gave Israel rest from their surrounding enemies in Joshua's lifetime.
Joshua summons all Israel together with their elders, heads, judges, and officers.
Joshua calls Israel's elders and other leaders to the national assembly at Shechem.
Joshua addresses all the people with a declaration from the LORD, their national God.
Balak fought against Israel and summoned Balaam to curse the people addressed as you.
Joshua urges the people to turn their hearts to the LORD, whom they call our God.
Israel served the LORD throughout Joshua's lifetime and that of the surviving elders.
The elders knew the works the LORD had done for Israel during Joshua's era.
Judah invites Simeon to fight the Canaanites in their allotted tribal territories.
Simeon joins Judah in the campaign to conquer their tribal allotments.
The wilderness of Judah is the territory where the Kenites settle with Judah's descendants.
Simeon accompanies Judah, and together they destroy the Canaanite inhabitants of Zephath.
Manasseh fails to dispossess the Canaanite inhabitants of towns in its tribal territory.
Israel becomes strong and subjects the remaining Canaanites to forced labor.
Ephraim fails to drive out Gezer's Canaanites, who remain among the tribe.
Zebulun leaves Canaanite inhabitants in its towns and makes them tributaries.
Asher fails to expel the towns' inhabitants, and the next verse identifies the settlers as Asherites.
Naphtali lives among the Canaanites and receives tribute from the remaining towns' inhabitants.
